A view of a Nepal Railway train stands at a station platform as preparations gather pace for the proposed Janakpur–Ayodhya train service. | Photo Credit: ANI
In a bid to boost connectivity and bilateral ties with Nepal, the Ministry of Railways has launched Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham weekly express . Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh to Janakpur in Nepal, from Delhi on Monday (November 23, 2026).
The weekly train will establish a crucial rail link between two pilgrimage sites, namely Janakpur Dham and Ayodhya, believed to be the birthplace of Sita and Ram. Further, the initiative is expected to enhance trade and cultural ties between both countries.

The train will cover a distance of approximately 604 kilometres in 19 hours, passing through several important towns in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh . The weekly train will commence its journey from Janakpur Dham on Saturday, and from Ayodhya Cantt on Monday.
The express train will commence regular service from November 28. The originating train (15596) from India is scheduled to depart from its station at Ayodhya Cantt. at 5:50 p.m every Monday, and reach the final destination at Janakpur at 12:40 p.m. (Nepali time) next day. On its return journey, the train will leave Janakpur Dham at 1.10 pm (Nepali time) every Saturday and reach Ayodhya Cantt at 8.10 am on Sundays. The train is scheduled to halt at 10 stations as part of its itinerary.
Here is the list of stations where the train will have stoppages besides its terminal stations.
The Saryu-Kamala Express will be operated using modern 17-coach LHB (Linke Hofmann Busch) rakes. The train configuration includes eight air-conditioned coaches, seven sleeper-class coaches, one LSLRD (LHB Second Class, Luggage, Brake, and Disabled-friendly) coach, and one LWLRRM (LHB Power Car/Generator-cum-Luggage-cum-Brake Van) coach.
The ticket prices for the Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham weekly express are yet to be announced on the IRCTC website.
Indian citizens going to Nepal don’t need a visa if they have a valid passport.
Train services from India are conducted to neighbouring countries of Bangladesh and Nepal.
